prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence for specific kinds of changes is still thin, as each category has only one completed test so far.
No clear effect was seen for reordering sign-in steps (sign_in, reorder).
No clear effect was seen for introducing new flows on the home/waiting screen (home, new_flow).
Predictions have consistently been too high compared to measured results.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- home, new_flow: +0.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +0.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, redesign] Interactive Desktop Pet Controls Walkthrough: Redesigns the home_intro screen into a checklist layout where users practice moving, hiding, and talking to their desktop pet before finishing onboarding. (why: Support emails show frequent confusion after onboarding on how to control or hide pets, and the finish step has a low conversion rate of 64.8%.)
1: [choose_path, redesign] Split Card Path Selection Layout: Redesigns choose_path layout into side-by-side comparative cards with time estimates for quick pre-made pets versus custom creation. (why: The choose_path step has a mean duration of 514s and drop-off (76.2% conversion), indicating user hesitation during initial path selection.)
2: [sign_in, hint] Account Persistence & Sync Warning Hint: Adds an explicit explanatory hint on the sign-in screen informing users how logging in preserves and syncs pet data across sessions. (why: 8 support emails (the largest complaint category) involved users losing or resetting pets after signing in again.)
3: [adoption, incentive] Personality Trait Choice Cards: Adds interactive personality trait choice cards to the pet selection screen so users can personalize their pet's behavior. (why: Adoption stage has the lowest overall conversion (60.9%), requiring stronger user affinity and engagement during friend selection.)
4: [home, wait_info] Render Stage Time Estimate & Progress Bar: Enables detailed progress percentage and estimated time remaining indicators on the waiting screen. (why: The waiting step has a long median of 201s and mean of 2336s, causing user uncertainty about whether rendering is stuck.)
5: [finish, layout] Spotlight Desktop Controls Guide: Changes the home_intro screen to a spotlight layout focusing on desktop tray and pet interaction shortcuts. (why: Multiple support emails mention confusion regarding how to hide, summon, or talk to the pet after completing onboarding.)
6: [choose_path, notification] Desktop Notification Opt-In Prompt: Adds a desktop notification option to the introductory story screen so users get notified when pet processing finishes. (why: Extremely high mean times across adoption (1017s) and home (2336s) suggest users switch away while waiting and forget to return.)
7: [adoption, copy] Reassuring Adoption Certificate Confirmation Copy: Updates adoption certificate headline and body text to clearly confirm pet creation success and set expectations for desktop launch. (why: Adoption completion drops significantly to 60.9%, needing clear confirmation copy to reassure users before the waiting phase.)

scores.note: High drop at finish step (35.2%) supported by user emails, but complex redesign carries execution risk.
Target step drops 23.8% with long duration, but lacks support email evidence.
Directly targets largest support complaint category with low-cost hint copy.
Adoption has lowest conversion rate (60.9%), though requiring new interactive screen elements.
Addresses high median/mean waiting time on home, though past home changes yielded modest results.
High drop at finish supported by support feedback, easier to implement than full walkthrough.
Addresses high idle time across adoption and home, but relies on user granting notification permissions.
Target step is the biggest funnel bottleneck, and fix is simple copy configuration.
